topic: Animal and Plant Cells and Organelles
key_concepts: All organisms are made of cells.
The cell is the smallest basic structural and functional unit of an organism.
Robert Hooke first used the term cell after observing cork under a microscope.
Animal cells have three major parts: cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus.
The cell membrane controls what enters and exits the cell.
Cytoplasm is a jelly-like fluid where organelles are embedded.
The nucleus controls and regulates cell activities and contains DNA.
Organelles are membrane-bound structures with specific functions.
Mitochondria produce energy and are known as the powerhouse of the cell.
Ribosomes are made of RNA and function in protein synthesis.
Lysosomes clean up cell waste products.
Plant cells have a cell wall that protects and supports the cell.
